findings.title: test_share_knowledge.py tests a duplicated inline wrapper, not the actual tools.py implementation
findings.why_it_matters: The ShareKnowledgeTool class (lines 9-57) is an inline reimplementation of the logic in plugins/share_knowledge/tools.py. It duplicates scope enforcement, write/query/delete logic, and SQLite interaction. Tests pass against this wrapper but provide ZERO confidence that the actual production code works. If tools.py has a bug (e.g., in _check_scope, _resolve_db_path, _ensure_schema, or the actual SQL queries), no test would catch it. This is worse than no test because it signals coverage while providing none.

tools.py has 311 lines of production code with scope config loading, DB path validation, schema resolution, and profile identity — none exercised by tests
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the inline ShareKnowledgeTool wrapper with direct calls to _handle_share_knowledge from plugins.share_knowledge.tools. Use a test-scoped db_path via the db_path fixture and pass scope_config dicts to test scope enforcement. This will test the actual production code path including _resolve_db_path, _ensure_schema, _get_calling_profile, _check_scope, _write, _query, and _delete.

residual_risks: The test_share_knowledge.py wrapper class may have diverged from tools.py implementation — any behavioral difference between the wrapper and the real code is completely invisible to tests
Dashboard auth middleware is registered in the app but never tested — a misconfigured middleware could block all requests or allow unauthenticated access in production

Revolt adapter's WebSocket reconnection loop (_run_websocket) has complex error handling (auth errors stop reconnecting, rate limits wait, other errors backoff) — if this logic is wrong, the bot could either stop reconnecting on transient errors or infinite-loop on auth failures

Supervisor lifecycle uses subprocess.Popen to launch hermes CLI — if the CLI interface changes or hermes is not installed, all profile management fails silently. No test verifies the subprocess command format
Zeus chip_in uses asyncio.run() inside a synchronous function (handle_chip_in) — this will fail if called from an already-running event loop. No test exercises this edge case
Dashboard seed_data.py writes to ~/.hermes/olympus.db by default — running tests could corrupt production data if the DB path isn't overridden. No test verifies the path override mechanism
The integration tests that require Hermes (TestProfileBoot, TestPluginLoading) are skipped when Hermes isn't installed — in CI without Hermes, ~15 tests are silently skipped, giving false green
Revolt adapter depends on gateway.config and gateway.platforms.base modules that are external to this repo — no test verifies the adapter correctly implements the BasePlatformAdapter interface
testing_gaps: No unit tests for any plugin code — all tests are either structural checks (file exists, string in file) or direct SQLite queries that bypass the actual application code
